question: Does the slow 11-burst top-off deliver more when the same pump has just poured a full glass?
programs: topoff_n11 (ratio 18, 11 bursts of 51 ms, 494 ms gaps) and steady_glass (ratio 19, 14 bursts of 215 ms) from programs.json, with their frozen forecasts from model-used.json, both copied unchanged from the record at 37aec3c88.
rested: First, before any glass and with no pour on either head since the park at 13:32: topoff_n11 on A then on B, from its start level, twice.
cycles: Set the cup to steady_glass's start level. A pours steady_glass, waits the cycle's delay, pours topoff_n11. Then B pours steady_glass, waits the same delay, pours topoff_n11. B's glass and top-off return the cup for A's, so each cycle tests both heads with no positioning gate between a glass and its top-off.
delay_definition: From the glass's finishing photograph to the top-off's first motor command. Delay 0 is as soon as a fresh stream, its no-pump bracket and its starting photograph allow; the journal records each actual interval.
skip_rule: A cycle that cannot finish by last_cycle_end_local is skipped. The second delay-120 cycle goes first, then the second delay-0 cycle. The single delay-300 cycle is the one-repeat condition.
settling_correction: Each top-off's stream takes a no-pump photograph, waits bracket_s (about the top-off's pour plus its settling wait), then the starting photograph, the pour and the finishing photograph. The level change between the first two, scaled to the start-to-finish interval and taken in the pump's direction, is the settling estimate. Corrected dose = raw dose minus that estimate. Both are reported.
response: Settling-corrected dose on the x990 sightline; x1986 reported beside it.
noise_basis: Reader noise on x990 is under 0.01 mL per photograph (results/reader-validation.json at 37aec3c88). A's repeat spread on rested 11-burst top-offs at 37aec3c88 was 0.08 mL standard deviation, up to 0.28 on other top-off variants. 0.5 mL is about twice the largest of those; 1.0 mL is the practical tolerance. The effect under test, read from one pour per head, is about 3 mL.

rule_per_head.D: mean corrected after-glass dose at a delay minus mean corrected rested dose, same head.
rule_per_head.supported: D at delay 0 is at least 1.0 mL and every delay-0 repeat exceeds the rested mean by more than 0.5 mL.
rule_per_head.ruled_out: D is below 0.5 mL at every delay tested.

B_caveat: B switched between two short-burst yields at 37aec3c88, with repeat spreads up to about 2.7 mL on one top-off variant. B is scored by the same rule and its spread is reported beside it.

amendment.registered_before: Registered after the original plan was stopped before its first measured pour (two positioning gates ran) and before any part of this amendment ran. It replaces the original order; the delay cycles run afterwards only if time remains, under the original deadline.
amendment.question: Does the raised top-off seen at 13:27:56 come back when the event before it is repeated?
amendment.order: 1. Rested: topoff_n11 on A then B, twice, before any glass. 2. Three steady_glass pairs (A then B) back to back, the pause, then topoff_n11 on A then B, then a second topoff_n11 pair at once; twice, once with positioning gates on A during the pause (gates true) and once without (gates false, the top-off starts where the glasses left the cup). 3. One steady_glass pair, the same pause, the same two top-off pairs, without gates.
amendment.pause_definition: From the return of the last glass's measurement (its finishing photograph) to the first top-off's motor start, matching 13:26:15 to about 13:27:49 in the record at 37aec3c88. Each top-off keeps the no-pump bracket and settling correction above.

raised_cut.basis: Corrected x990 dose of an 11-burst top-off. This morning A's unraised 11-burst top-offs ran 5.24 to 6.08 mL and its raised ones 7.4 to 8.7 overnight and 8.47 today; B's unraised ran 4.75 to 5.58 and its raised ones 6.59 to 7.48.

amendment.rule: On each head, the first top-off after three glasses: raised in two of two episodes supports a run of glasses as the cause; raised in none of two rules the glasses out as a reliable cause; one of two is unresolved. A's base rate of a raised 11-burst top-off this session is about one pour in thirty. The second top-off pair and the one-glass episode are reported against the same cut without a separate ruling.
